name: mark_point
description:
Measure up to eight visible pixels of one current RGB view as world-frame points in a single call.
Use when: one or more exact pixels — not an object identity, centre or full extent — must become world XYZ for a waypoint, clearance comparison or geometric fallback. Pass point_ids and points_uv index-aligned and of equal length, in the native top-left [x,y] coordinates of the named view, choosing pixels well inside the intended visible surface. For one pixel, pass one point_id and one points_uv entry in the same batch format.
Effect: read-only with respect to the world, but every measured pixel persists one observation-bound geometric mark under its point_id. Reusing a name already solved from another view verifies the new measurement against the stored one instead of replacing it; a disagreement beyond 25 mm fails only that entry, with error_code inconsistent_mark, and keeps the stored measurement.
Returns: a call status of solved, partial or failed, plus one marks[] entry per requested pixel in request order, each repeating its own source_index. An entry carries its own status, xyz_m in metres when it solved, the distinct views that measured that name, and its depth-support evidence — measured depth, window radius, valid, supporting and rejected sample counts, and maximum support deviation — on success and on failure alike. The call returns one composite overlay: each entry names the colour_rgb it was drawn in, and image_mapping binds a panel to a source_index rather than to its position, because inline images are evicted one block at a time. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured.
Does not: track a pixel through robot or camera motion, segment or identify the object, infer hidden geometry, correct a click on the wrong surface, expose simulator ground truth, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or success. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, not an object centre, and eight measured pixels are not a shape.
On error: Refused: a call with more than eight entries, point_ids and points_uv of unequal lengths, a repeated or empty name, a name longer than 64 characters, a negative pixel coordinate, or a view that cannot be marked; the whole call is refused and the refusal names the field. A pixel that cannot be measured fails only its own entry and leaves the rest solved. Read that entry's error_code: aim farther inside the surface for depth_discontinuity or insufficient_depth_support, choose a different pixel for invalid_depth at the camera far plane, and resolve a disputed name from a complementary current view. A wrist camera moves with its arm, so after any motion discard old wrist pixels and query the fresh observation rather than hand-projecting the old image location.

point_ids.description: One to eight stable names, index-aligned with points_uv: point_ids[i] names the geometric point measured at points_uv[i]. Must have the same length as points_uv or the whole call is rejected. Names must be distinct within one call: reusing a name already solved in this round from another view verifies it against the stored measurement, which is meaningless against a second pixel of the same image.

items.description: One short stable name for this geometric point, at most 64 characters, for example "mug_rim_left". Dimensionless identifier, not a coordinate.

points_uv.description: One to eight pixels to measure, index-aligned with point_ids and measured in array order. Must have the same length as point_ids or the whole call is rejected. Each pixel is measured independently: one pixel outside the image or without usable depth fails only its own entry and leaves the rest solved.

items.description: One pixel as [u,v] in integer pixels of the exact returned view, top-left OpenCV origin: u from the left edge, v from the top edge.
Non-negative pixel coordinate in the exact returned view's own resolution.

view.description: Exact returned current RGB view containing every pixel in this call. All [u,v] pairs are in this view's top-left OpenCV pixel frame at the resolution that view was returned at, and every resulting coordinate is in metres in the world frame. A wrist view is valid calibration only at its current post-motion pose: pixels read from a wrist view before it moved are not current geometry.

success.description: The call itself ran. It says nothing about whether any pixel measured: read status and each entry's own status.

status.description: solved: every entry produced a measurement or a pending constraint. partial: some entries failed and the rest stand. failed: no entry produced a measurement.

view.description: The single view every pixel of this call was read from.

observation_id.description: The observation these pixels and coordinates are bound to. Pixels from a different observation are not current geometry.

mark_count.description: Number of requested pixels, equal to len(marks).

solved_count.description: How many entries reached solved, verified or pending.

failed_count.description: How many entries failed and would need a new pixel.

marks.description: One entry per requested pixel, in request order and of the same length, each repeating its own source_index.

source_index.description: Zero-based index of the request entry this result measures: point_ids[source_index] and points_uv[source_index]. Present on every entry so attribution never depends on array position surviving delivery.

point_id.description: The requested name for this geometric point.

point_uv.description: The requested pixel [u,v] in integer pixels of the requested view, top-left OpenCV origin.

items.description: Pixel coordinate in the requested view.

status.description: solved: this call measured the point and stored it. verified: the name was already solved from another view and this measurement agreed with it. pending: a point-cloud click constrained some axes but not all three. failed: this pixel produced no measurement; the other entries are unaffected.

error_code.description: Null unless this entry failed. Names why this one pixel produced no measurement, using exactly the codes the single-pixel form raises for the same conditions: invalid_arguments for a pixel outside the view or a view that cannot be marked, invalid_depth at the camera far plane, insufficient_depth_support and depth_discontinuity near an edge, inconsistent_mark when two measurements of one name disagree by more than 25 mm, stale_point when the world moved under a pending name. error_message carries the distinction the shared code does not.

error_message.description: Null unless this entry failed. One sentence, at most 200 characters, naming the correction for this pixel.

xyz_m.description: World position [x,y,z] in metres, or null when this entry did not solve. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, not an object centre.

views.description: The distinct views this name has now been measured from, oldest first, at most the eight most recent. Dimensionless camera names.

items.description: One view name this measurement came from.

next_views.description: For a pending point-cloud mark, the complementary views that would still constrain the missing axes. Empty otherwise.

colour_rgb.description: The [r,g,b] colour, 0-255 per channel, that draws this mark in the composite overlay. This is the attribution carrier: it lives in the result body, so it survives even if the image is dropped from a later request. Null when nothing was drawn.

verification_distance_m.description: For a verified entry, the distance in metres between the stored measurement and this one; for a point-cloud verification, the largest per-axis disagreement in metres. Null otherwise.

quality_method.description: Which depth estimator produced this entry, or "not_measured" when the entry failed before any depth was read. Dimensionless identifier.

quality_status.description: measured: a supported local surface was found. partial: depth was read but rejected, and the counters below say why. unmeasured: the entry failed before depth was read.

quality_depth_m.description: Measured distance in metres along the camera's optical axis at this pixel, or null when no depth was accepted.

quality_window_radius_px.description: Radius in pixels of the square support window sampled around the pixel. Null when no depth was read.

quality_valid_samples.description: Count of finite in-range depth samples in that window. Null when no depth was read.

quality_supporting_samples.description: Count of those samples compatible with the clicked depth. A small count on a solved mark means a thin or grazing surface.

quality_rejected_samples.description: Count of window samples at an incompatible depth. A large count means the pixel sits near a silhouette.

quality_max_support_deviation_m.description: Largest deviation in metres between a supporting sample and the reported depth. Null when no depth was accepted.

action_workspace_inside.description: Whether the measured point lies inside the command envelope, or null when this surface does not report it. This is a command-envelope test, never a reachability, collision or grasp claim.

action_workspace_use.description: What the envelope test permits: a candidate still needing a motion preview, or a measurement outside the envelope. Null when this surface does not report it.

items.description: One measurement attempt: its own source_index, the name and pixel it was asked for, its outcome, and the depth evidence behind it.

image_mapping.description: What each returned image shows, bound by source_index rather than by position.

image_index.description: Position of this image among the images returned by this call.

role.description: mark_batch_panel: one view with every solved mark of this call drawn in its own colour_rgb and a colour legend.

camera.description: The view this panel renders. Dimensionless name.

source_index.description: The request entry this image depicts, or null when the panel depicts several marks at once. Never infer it from position: inline images are dropped one block at a time, so a surviving image may no longer sit where it was returned.

candidate_id.description: Always null: mark_point measures a pixel, it does not select a candidate. Present so every perception tool's image binding has one shape.

target_ref.description: Always null: a mark is a coordinate, not a target reference. Present so every image binding has one shape.

observation_step.description: Observation step this panel was rendered from, or null when the step is not carried.

items.description: One returned image and what it depicts, bound by source_index rather than by its position.

measurement_contract.description: Units and evidence boundary for these measurements, added by surfaces that deliver it.
